The present petition has been filed by the petitioner under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking grant of bail in Case FIR No.106/2023 dated 31.05.2023, registered under Sections 341, 342, 363, 376 & 120-B of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 at Police Station, Bhunter, District Kullu, Himachal Pradesh.

sentences.text: Status report stands filed.
The same is taken on record.
Copy, whereof, has been supplied to learned counsel for the petitioner.

3. The brief facts are that on 31.05.2023, the father of the victim had moved an application informing the Police that his daughter (victim), who was studying in 8th Class at Global School Hurla has not returned home.
Whether reporters of Local Papers may be allowed to see the judgment?
The victim in the case at hand was born on 15.03.2011.
Initially, the FIR was registered for commission of offences punishable under Sections 363, 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.

The victim was traced on .
01.06.2023 by her parents and thereafter she was brought to the Police Station.
In the Police Station, statement of the victim under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was recorded.
Subsequent thereto, the victim was got medically examined at C.H. Tegu-behar in presence of her mother.
4. The Medico Legal Certificate (MLC) and other preservatives taken by the Medical Officer were obtained.

The victim, in her statement, disclosed that on the call of the juvenile in conflict with law,
she went to Garsa in Bhuvneshwari bus.
At Garsa, the juvenile in conflict with law called one Amit on telephone.
The victim was willing to return home, but she was withheld by the juvenile in conflict with law.
At about 8:00 p.m., the juvenile in conflict with law took the victim to the quarter of the bail petitioner.

In the said quarter, the victim stayed till 8:00 a.m. on 01.06.2023.
5.
On 02.06.2023, statement of the victim was recorded under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Lahaul & Spiti at Kullu.
The father of the victim informed the Police that he had a doubt that something wrong had happened with the victim as he had noticed her abnormal behaviour.

A supplementary statement of the complainant was recorded on 03.06.2023.
6.
On 30.08.2023, a supplementary statement of the victim was recorded once again under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

In the said statement, she disclosed that on 31.05.2023 at .
about 8:00-9:00 p.m., the bail petitioner had done a wrong act with her.
Statement of the victim under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was again recorded in the Court, in which the victim gave the same version.
7. After receipt of the medical opinion and reports, Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code were added.

sentences.text: The bail petitioner was arrested by the Police on 06.09.2023.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the record.
9. The Challan in the case at hand was presented before the Court on 02.11.2023 and now the case is listed for consideration of charge on 31.05.2024.
10. The nature of accusation in the case at hand is serious.
Besides, the statements of the victim made under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, directly implicate the bail petitioner.

Other than the aforeaid, as per the report of Regional Forensic State Laboratory, Mandi, semen stains detected on the sweater of the victim and the bed-sheet, have .
matched with the DNA of the present bail petitioner.
The punishment in the case at hand is severe.

11. Besides the aforesaid, in terms of Section 29 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, when a person is prosecuted for committing an offence under Section 3 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, then it is presumed that the person had committed the offence.

sentences.text: Hence, in the case at hand, the presumption of innocence does not exist in favour of the present bail petitioner, rather the burden of proving that the offence in the case at hand was not committed, now squarely lies upon the petitioner.
12. For framing of charge, the case is listed before the trial Court on 31.05.2024.
In all, there are 27 witnesses to be examined in the case at hand, out of which, 15 are the official witnesses.
13. Keeping in view the aforesaid facts and attending circumstances, I do not find it expedient to enlarge the petitioner on bail, at this stage.
Accordingly, the present petition is dismissed.
14. The observations made herein above shall remain confined to the disposal of the present petition only and will have no bearing, whatsoever, on the merits of the case.

( Bipin Chander Negi)
